title: Static Wide-Head Branched-Gill Fin-Tail Axolotl
description: One newly authored complete static axolotl-like amphibian display. A broad low blunt head flows into an elongated low body and one laterally curved narrow muscular tail with a tall finite upper/lower fin envelope integral to the same closed whole skin. Three outward-upward thick branched gill-like fans on each side of the head have genuine open outline clefts and finite material branches, not painted tufts. Four short bent limbs end in separately whole thick splayed cleft feet on finite ground soles, with small lateral dark eyes and no external ears. All whole stations, limb/foot outlines and gill profiles newly authored; not an old tadpole enlarged and given old frog feet. One model, zero scenes; fixed artistic opaque exterior only, no exact species, microscopic gill filaments, developmental stage, respiration, aquatic operation, animation or anatomy certification.
